chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام), who said:

I heard him saying: “There is no year less in rain than another year, but Allah places it where He wills. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when a people act with acts of disobedience, diverts from them what had been decreed for them of rain in that year to others besides them, and to the deserts, the seas, and the mountains. And indeed Allah surely punishes the dung beetle in its hole by withholding rain from the land in whose place it is, because of the sins of those in its vicinity; and Allah has made for it a path in a route other than the quarter of the people of disobedience.”
He said: Then Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام) said: “So take a lesson, O people of insight.”

key_terms.الْجُعَلَ: the dung beetle; cited as a creature affected by withheld rain
key_terms.الْفَيَافِي: deserts or open wastelands; places to which rain may be redirected
key_terms.بِالْمَعَاصِي: through acts of disobedience; the cause of deprivation mentioned here
key_terms.بِخَطَايَا: because of sins; indicating moral causation in the narration
key_terms.سَنَةٍ: a year; the measure by which rainfall is being compared
key_terms.فَاعْتَبِرُوا: take a lesson; a direct exhortation to reflect and heed the warning
key_terms.قَدَّرَ: decreed; what Allah had apportioned or ordained
key_terms.مَطَرًا: rain; the divine provision discussed in the hadith

ai.seo_question: How do sins affect rainfall and divine blessings according to Imam Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that rainfall is not inherently diminished from one year to another; rather, Allah distributes it wherever He wills. It warns that collective sins can cause blessings to be diverted from a people, making the narration a moral exhortation about the worldly effects of disobedience and a call to reflection.
